t: A dirt-cheap RISC-V chip for tiny light, button, and sensor gadgets.
steps: Buy a nanoCH32V003 board bundled with a WCH-LinkE programmer from MuseLab on Tindie, or an Olimex board from Olimex.
Connect the WCH-LinkE to the board with the power, ground and single debug wire.
Plug the WCH-LinkE into your computer with a USB cable.
Install the free Arduino IDE and add the WCH board package, or set up the ch32fun SDK with a RISC-V compiler.
Upload the blink example and watch the board LED flash.
Try a ch32fun example for color LEDs next.
Leave the debug pin free in your projects to keep programming working.
meta: Open Board. From $1.50. A few stores.
